svg.aria-label: One-sample t-test teaching board for the cupcake audit

text.tspan: One sample of calories compared with one fixed claim: μ0 = 200 calories. R-based audit, uncertainty, p-values, CIs, and power.
From label claim to one-sample test
Cafe claim: average cupcake calories are 200.
The unit of evidence is the sample mean, not
The gap exists, but variation sets the scale
Measured calories, one cupcake per day
214.4 is above 200. The t-test asks whether 14.4 calories is large
after accounting for s = 20.9 and n = 10.
Code, mock output, and reproducible figures
# do not reject H0 at alpha = 0.05
In class, run the code, then ask which quantity changed
the verdict when n grew from 10 to 30.
Give the cafe the benefit of the doubt
If H0 were true, individual cupcakes vary around 200.
The test asks how unusual this sample mean would be in that null world.
Convert the calorie gap into standard errors
How far into the t tails did the sample land?
Same mean, more data, stronger evidence
More cupcakes shrink SE, not the observed story
Mental model: sample statistics estimate uncertainty.
The null t distribution translates distance into evidence.
α split across both tails, cautious default
More power, but direction must be chosen before data
How to state the result without overstating it
remains plausible with only ten cupcakes.
Claim to verdict to next sample
Teaching close: the mean barely changed from n=10 to n=30, but uncertainty fell. That is power.
